PullRequest.Title: Add JUnit reporter for unit tests
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please: 
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/Microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests.
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `master` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them. 
-->

This PR fixes #103814

Scenarios.Scenario: Electron unit tests in Azure Pipelines with --tfs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The renderer loads and runs the complete unit-test set, forwards Mocha lifecycle events to the main process over Electron IPC, and completion then waits for end-event listeners before the subsequent 'all done' IPC causes app exit. JUnit report construction/output is therefore on the completion path, after the tests themselves.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward Mocha suite, test, hook, pass/fail, and completion events from renderer to main process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Several IPC messages per test/hook plus suite events for the full test run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPCReporter/IPCRunner event forwarding already fed the Spec reporter before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Events carry reporting state during test execution and the final end/all-done ordering gates process exit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Accumulate/format Mocha results into JUnit XML through the reporter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One XML report per Electron invocation, containing the full effective test set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: With --tfs, only Spec output was produced; JUnit reporter construction was commented out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reporter end handling occurs before the later all-done exit message can complete the run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write the JUnit XML artifact under BUILD_ARTIFACTSTAGINGDIRECTORY when that environment variable is set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One report file per platform/suite invocation, not one file per test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This Electron unit-test path did not write a JUnit artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The report must be finalized at test end for publication before app exit.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One reporter receives one pass/fail/pending event per executed test in the full unit-test set. The report's CPU, retained test metadata, and bytes scale linearly with test count and failure detail size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One Electron test process and one JUnit reporter per pipeline test invocation. Test lifecycle IPC is serialized through Electron's event channel; report generation is not fanned out per test into filesystem writes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or deduplication applies. Each CI invocation is cold and creates a fresh report; the configured artifact filename is one stable file per platform and suite invocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the diff adds linear report serialization/retention and one artifact write on --tfs runs; low that this bounded, intentional work causes a regression beyond the reporting feature's expected cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository pins Electron 7.3.2, while the deleted note documented a hang specifically with Electron 6 in a Docker container; there is no current trace or implementation evidence proving that old hang persists. Exact XML generation and write duration is also not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added work is the requested report generation, has one filesystem output per run, and does not create per-test boundary fan-out or uncontrolled concurrency. The obsolete Electron 6 hang note alone is insufficient to prove a current Electron 7 performance failure.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browser unit tests explicitly run with --tfs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each selected Playwright browser is launched, loads the test page, runs the module set, and forwards Mocha events through the exposed page function. The JUnit reporter handles those events and finalizes its report before that browser run closes; all selected browser promises must settle before the command exits.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch one Playwright browser process for each selected browser type.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One launch per selected browser, three by default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same browsers were launched concurrently before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All browser runs must complete before command exit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward browser-context Mocha events to the Node process through Playwright's exposed-function bridge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Several bridge calls per test/hook plus suite events, independently for each selected browser.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same bridge fed the selected Mocha reporter before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reporting events are part of each browser test run's progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build JUnit report data for each browser's complete test run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One report per selected browser; three reports under the default browser selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: --tfs did not previously select a JUnit reporter in the browser harness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each report is finalized at that browser's end event before all browser promises settle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write a browser-specific JUnit XML artifact when BUILD_ARTIFACTSTAGINGDIRECTORY is present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file per selected browser due to browserType in the filename; three concurrent end-of-run outputs by default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No JUnit artifact was written by this harness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each browser report is completion work, but there is no per-test filesystem fan-out.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective test count per browser controls report size and reporter CPU. With the default selection, the same module set runs in chromium, firefox, and webkit, yielding three independently generated reports.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing browserTypes.map plus Promise.all runs up to three browser processes concurrently by default. The diff adds one reporter per browser but no additional browser/process concurrency; report finalization can overlap across those existing runs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No warm cache or cross-browser coalescing exists for test results. Each browser run produces independent data. When BUILD_ARTIFACTSTAGINGDIRECTORY is set, browserType is included in the filename so outputs do not overwrite each other.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that explicit --tfs runs add one linear report and one output per browser; high that process concurrency and event bridge cardinality are pre-existing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Official Linux browser pipeline commands shown in the repository do not pass --tfs, so prevalence is limited to explicit invocations or future pipeline wiring. Exact report size and end-of-run duration depend on selected modules and reporter internals.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Output cardinality is bounded and correctly partitioned by browser, and the diff does not amplify browser launch or IPC frequency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal local Electron and browser unit-test runs without --tfs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The harness starts, parses arguments, discovers/loads tests, launches Electron or selected Playwright browsers, and executes the suite. The JUnit reporter module is required during harness startup, but no JUnit reporter is constructed and no report is generated.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve and load the reporter package and its dependencies during harness startup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per Node/Electron main process due to the module cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Browser runs did not import the package; Electron had the import commented out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds a small fixed startup cost before tests can run, including when --tfs is absent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Glob and load the selected compiled test modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discovery pass followed by module loads for the selected test set.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The newly added startup work is a single module load per harness process and does not scale with test count, module count, events, or browser count within that process.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing Electron or Playwright process concurrency is unchanged. The eager require does not launch subprocesses or create per-test work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Node's module cache ensures the dependency is loaded at most once per harness process. There is no report cache because reporting is disabled.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the eager require is newly on startup; high that its multiplicity is one and no reporter work follows without --tfs.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The reporter package's exact cold-load latency and memory footprint are not measured, but it is a single cached dependency load relative to a full unit-test process.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Moving the require into the --tfs branch could avoid a minor fixed cost, but the diff provides no evidence of a concrete user-visible performance regression, so this would be speculative micro-optimization.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed both complete changed-file diffs and traced normal, Electron --tfs, and browser --tfs workflows through module loading, test-event IPC, concurrent browser execution, JUnit serialization, and artifact output. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was established, so no findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
